mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to be negative, encouraging equity investment and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the low-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts stronger labor market conditions, which are associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while HOUST rises by >5% in the following month
regime_hint: Expanding labor market with rising sentiment
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend suggests strengthening supply-side demand for capital goods, which is expected to boost equity valuations and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above its 12-month moving average
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO breakout and SPX 20-day forward returns (Pearson < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% indicates reduced upward price pressure, lowering policy uncertainty and increasing expected equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative and persistent across 10 such events.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% (implied by UNRATE), the expectation of job growth reduces risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to compression in equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during the low-unemployment window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in retail sales proxy (not available in the catalog; fallback to RSAFS as a demand proxy) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests shifting demand toward consumer goods, which can drive positive 60-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >5% while INDPRO decreases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 10 such demand shifts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in job openings (implied by PAYEMS trend) signals labor market softening, which is associated with increased uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >3% over 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1) during the cooling period.

mechanism_narrative: When supply chain disruptions (indirectly reflected by a combination of INDPRO and RSAFS both below trend) persist for 60 days, the uncertainty raises the cost of capital, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the same horizon.
failure_condition: 60-day SPX forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the disruption window.
